newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MARLINS EDGE BRAVES FOR FOURTH STRAIGHT WIN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MARLINS EDGE BRAVES FOR FOURTH STRAIGHT WIN.

text.p: Kurt Abbott doubled home the tying run in the top of the seventh inning and Edgar Renteria followed with an RBI single as the Florida Marlins held on for their fourth straight win, 4-3 over the Atlanta Braves on Wednesday.
Kevin Brown got the win, allowing three runs and seven hits in six innings. He helped himself by scoring twice, including the tie-breaking run in the seventh.
The Marlins have won six of their last seven games.
Kenny Lofton and Chipper Jones each had two hits and an RBI for Atlanta, which has lost five of its last six at home.
In Chicago, Nelson Liriano's two-run homer off Mel Rojas in the ninth inning lifted the Los Angeles Dodgers to a come-from-behind 6-4 victory over the Chicago Cubs.
Eric Anthony led off the ninth with a double off Rojas. After a sacrifice by Juan Castro, Liriano hit his first homer of the season to snap a 4-4 tie.
"I wanted Mel (Rojas) to throw a strike on the inside corner," Cubs catcher Scott Servais said. "The ball caught too much of the plate (and) you saw the results."
Raul Mondesi homered and drove in three runs for Los Angeles.
In Cincinnati, Barry Bonds' home run broke a tie in the top of the 10th inning and the San Francisco Giants defeated the Cincinnati Reds 4-2 for their fourth straight win.
Bonds hit a 2-1 pitch from Mike Remlinger 444 feet into the bleachers in right-centre field with one out in the 10th for his sixth homer of the season and second in three games.
Cincinnati, off to its worst in 47 years, has lost four straight and 20 of its last 26 games.
In Montreal, Rondell White's double in the eighth inning scored Mike Lansing with the go-ahead run as the Montreal Expos rallied past the slumping San Diego Padres 9-7 for their third straight win.
Montreal, which has won five of its last seven games, scored four times in the eighth inning off Padres closer Trevor Hoffman to erase a 7-5 deficit.
San Diego has lost six of its last nine games and 15 of its last 20.

In New York, Darryl Kile scattered four hits over eight innings and Craig Biggio's pinch sacrifice fly in the ninth inning scored Bill Spiers with the game's only run as the Houston Astros edged the New York Mets, 1-0.
In his last three starts, Kile has allowed one run and 13 hits in 24 innings for a 0.38 ERA.
"There is a calm about him now and it shows," Astros manager Larry Dierker said about Kile. "You used to be able to read the agitation in his face."
The Mets wasted a sterling effort by Rick Reed. He allowed five hits and one walk over eight scoreless innings

In Philadelphia, Micah Franklin collected his first major-league hit, home run and RBI and Gary Gaetti homered and drove in three runs as the St. Louis pounded out a season-high 17 hits in a 12-3 rout of the Philadelphia Phillies.
Franklin, playing in his second major-league game, singled in the second inning for his first career hit. He hit his first homer in the ninth off reliever Ken Ryan.
"This is like a dream come true, I didn't get any sleep when I heard I was being called up," Franklin said. "There will be a few phone calls home tonight."

In Pittsburgh, Kevin Young's pinch two-run double off reliever Steve Reed keyed a nine-run eighth inning as the Pittsburgh Pirates rallied for a 15-10 victory over the Colorado Rockies, snapping a three-game losing streak.
Al Martin capped the scoring in the eighth with his first career grand slam as the Pirates had their biggest inning in 11 years.
Pirates starter Esteban Loaiza, who entered the game with a 2.44 ERA, was chased after surrendering six runs in five innings.
